audit.recode_to: Drop 'fixed-strict' final (strict=True, dom=True, rule 01 001 0001...). Recode as kind 'conflict' (Ross & Paol 1978:2, hedged 'in general' final vs. the two dedicated SIL phonologies, which agree with each other against Ross), or, if the catalog resolves conflicts toward the dedicated phonology, as 'lexical' with strong positional tendencies (stress 'not fully predictable', low-functional-load contrasts; non-verbs predominantly INITIAL in 2-3-syllable words, second syllable in 4-syllable words, /r l s g/-onset second syllables often attract stress; verbs: future tense penultimate, other tenses disyllables initial, 3+ syllables always a stress on the final syllable with alternating stresses before it). prule should carry both statements; cite Barker & Lee n.d. [1976 data] sec. 3.3.1-3.3.2 pp.26-28 and Barker 1992 OPD p.3 alongside Ross 1978:2. Also fix the locator 'section 1.1 Phonology' -> 'section 1.1 General' and populate the empty top-level quote/cite/grade fields.
audit.reasoning: Quote check: confirmed verbatim in the held PL-B56 PDF at printed p.2 (PDF p.8), end of section 1.1 'General' (record's 'section 1.1 Phonology' label is slightly off; page is right). Deciding source is the standard and only published grammar (Ross & Paol 1978, PL B-56, grammar sketch), so the record rests on the best published description, and the coding (final stress, enclitics excluded, WORD domain) follows the text. Two caveats keep it below 'well-sourced': (a) Ross himself calls stress weak and the rules in need of further investigation and says final stress holds 'in general', so 'fixed-strict' is a strong reading of a hedged statement and the empty grade field should reflect that; (b) a dedicated 40-pp SIL phonology (Lee & Barker, archive 31253) and a 1992 OPD (42492) exist with open PDFs that I located but could not download (Cloudflare 403 from our machine
